onset.Description: Onset of the fixation, relative to the onset of the SEARCH DISPLAY on that trial. This departs from the BIDS convention of run-relative onsets: the raw files record only per-trial timings, so a run-relative onset could be produced only by assuming fixed inter-trial intervals. Trial-relative onset is the quantity that was measured and the one every analysis uses. Negative values occur for fixations already in progress when the display appeared.

trial.Description: Trial number within the session, starting at 1.

phase.Description: Which part of the trial the fixation falls in.

Levels.preview: During the fixation dot and preview, before the search display.

trial_type.Description: Preview condition, taken from the runtime record of which image was actually drawn as the preview, not from the stimulus filename.

Levels.preview: The scene was previewed before the search display.
Levels.no_preview: A grey placeholder was shown instead.

stim_file.Description: Scene shown on this trial, relative to the stimuli directory.

fixation_index.Description: Position of this fixation within its phase, starting at 1.

gaze_x.Description: Mean horizontal gaze position during the fixation, in screen pixels.

gaze_y.Description: Mean vertical gaze position during the fixation, in screen pixels.

is_detection.Description: 1 for the fixation that ended the trial by landing on the face. The display was gaze-contingent, so this fixation defines the detection latency. Always 0 on timeout trials, where the face was never fixated.

trial_duration.Description: Duration of the search display on this trial.

timeout.Description: 1 if the search display ran to its limit without the face being fixated (6 s in the face detection task, 20 s in the moving-window task). These trials have no detection latency and are excluded from every analysis.
